questions.prompt: I ___ a new job last month.
questions.explain: “Last month” is a finished time, so we use the past simple: started.

questions.prompt: Since January, I ___ English twice a week.
questions.explain: “Since” + something that is still happening → present perfect continuous: have been studying.

questions.prompt: Recently, I've ___ (move) to a new flat.
questions.explain: After I've (I have) we use the past participle: moved.

questions.prompt: How have things ___ for you?
questions.explain: “How have things been?” is a friendly way to ask for someone's news.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to what it does.
pairs: One thing that has changed is…
What has changed for you recently?
questions.explain: These are the four key moves of a personal update: the change, the reason, when it started, and a question back.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: since summer i've been walking more
i've been walking more since summer
questions.explain: Since summer, I've been walking more. (I've been walking more since summer is also correct.)

questions.prompt: Your friend says: “I've just changed jobs.” What's the best reply?
options: Oh really? How are you finding it so far?
questions.explain: A friendly reaction plus a follow-up question keeps the conversation going.

questions.passage: Hi Sara! Lots of news. I've moved to Milan for work, and since May I've been learning to cook because I live alone now. It's been tiring, but I'm enjoying it.
questions.prompt: Why has she been learning to cook?
questions.explain: “…I've been learning to cook because I live alone now.”

questions.prompt: Have you ever ___ a marathon?
questions.explain: “Have you ever…?” + past participle. Run → ran → run.

questions.prompt: I ___ to Japan twice.
questions.explain: “Have been” means you went and came back — a life experience. “Have gone” means you are still there.

questions.prompt: It ___ me three months to finish the course.
questions.explain: “It took me + time + to…” says how long something needed.

questions.prompt: One achievement I'm proud ___ is learning to swim.
questions.explain: We say “proud of something”.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to what it does.
pairs: It took me a year to…
What are you most proud of?
questions.explain: Use these to tell the story of an achievement: the chance, the effort, the lesson — and ask about theirs.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to make a question.
answers: have you ever baked a cake
questions.explain: Have you ever baked a cake?

questions.prompt: Your friend says: “I finally passed my driving test!” What's the best reply?
options: Congratulations! How many times did you try?
questions.explain: Show you're happy for them, then ask a follow-up question.

questions.passage: Last year Marco decided to learn the guitar. It took him six months to play his first full song. He says he learned that a little practice every day works better than long sessions at the weekend.
questions.prompt: What did Marco learn?
questions.explain: “…a little practice every day works better than long sessions at the weekend.”

questions.prompt: ___, we got lost, but then a kind man helped us.
questions.explain: “At first” introduces the beginning of the story.

questions.prompt: Which phrase tells the listener how the story finished?
questions.explain: “In the end” introduces the final result.

questions.prompt: It happened ___ I was on holiday in Sicily.
questions.explain: “It happened when…” sets the scene: where and when.

questions.prompt: After ___, we went for a pizza.
questions.explain: “After that” moves the story to the next event.

questions.prompt: Match each question to what it asks about.
questions.explain: Good listeners ask about the setting, the events, the feelings and the result.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: i felt nervous when it started
when it started i felt nervous
questions.explain: I felt nervous when it started. (When it started, I felt nervous is also correct.)

questions.prompt: I ___ home when it started to rain.
questions.explain: Past continuous (was walking) for the background action; past simple (started) for the event.

questions.passage: It happened when I was at the airport. At first, everything was fine. Then they announced that my flight was cancelled. After that, I waited for six hours. In the end, I got a seat on a later flight and arrived at midnight.
questions.prompt: What happened in the end?
options: She took a later flight and arrived at midnight
questions.explain: “In the end, I got a seat on a later flight and arrived at midnight.”

sets.title: Challenges and how you handled them

questions.prompt: The hardest part ___ finding a flat near my office.
questions.explain: “The hardest part” is singular and in the past here → was.

questions.prompt: So I ___ to ask my manager for help.
questions.explain: Past story → past simple: decided.

questions.prompt: It worked ___ because everyone helped.
questions.explain: “It worked out” = it finished well.

questions.prompt: If it happened again, I ___ plan better. (would / will)
questions.explain: “If it happened again, I would…” talks about an imaginary situation.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to what it does.
pairs: How did you deal with it?
questions.explain: These four moves tell a challenge story clearly.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: how did you deal with it
questions.explain: How did you deal with it?

questions.prompt: Your colleague says: “My laptop broke the day before my presentation.” Best reply?
options: Oh no! What did you do?
questions.explain: Show sympathy, then ask a follow-up question.

questions.prompt: Which word means the same as “deal with”?
questions.explain: Deal with = handle = manage a problem.

questions.prompt: I was really ___ when I heard the good news.
questions.explain: -ed adjectives describe how a person feels: relieved.

questions.prompt: The film was so ___ that I fell asleep.
questions.explain: -ing adjectives describe the thing that causes the feeling: boring.

questions.prompt: I felt nervous ___ it was my first day.
questions.explain: Give the reason with “because”.

questions.prompt: It made me ___ that family is important. (realise / realize)
questions.explain: “It made me realise…” says what you understood.

questions.prompt: Match each feeling to a situation.
pairs: the exam was easier than expected
a friend arrived without telling you
questions.explain: Linking feelings to situations helps you explain your reactions.

questions.prompt: Your friend says: “I didn't get the job.” Best reply?
options: Oh, that sounds disappointing. Are you OK?
questions.explain: “That sounds…” shows you understand how they feel.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: i was surprised by the news
questions.explain: I was surprised by the news.

questions.prompt: What was your ___ when you saw the result?
questions.explain: We need a noun here: reaction.

questions.prompt: I ___ live in Naples, but now I live in Rome.
questions.explain: Used to + verb = a past habit or situation that isn't true now.

questions.prompt: Did you ___ play football at school?
questions.explain: In questions and negatives we write “use to” (without -d): Did you use to…?

questions.prompt: Compared ___ before, I'm much busier now.
questions.explain: “Compared with/to before…” introduces a comparison.

questions.prompt: I've ___ more patient since I had children. (become)
questions.explain: Become → became → become. I've become = present perfect.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to what it does.
questions.explain: Use these to compare your life before and now.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: i didn't use to drink coffee
questions.explain: I didn't use to drink coffee. In negatives: didn't use to (no -d).

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explain: I used to smoke = I smoked in the past, but not now.

questions.prompt: What has changed the most? — “The most important difference is that I work from home now.” What is the change?
questions.explain: “I work from home now” — the place of work changed.

questions.prompt: Which question asks for more detail?
options: Could you tell me a little more about it?
questions.explain: “Could you tell me a little more about…?” invites a longer answer.

questions.prompt: Which question asks about the effect?
questions.explain: “How did that affect you?” asks about the result for the person.

questions.prompt: What happened ___ that?
questions.explain: “What happened after that?” asks about the next event.

questions.prompt: What do you ___ by “a busy week”?
questions.explain: “What do you mean by…?” asks for explanation.

questions.prompt: Match each question to what it asks for.
pairs: Why was that important to you?
questions.explain: Different follow-up questions ask for different information.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: That's interesting. How about you? — react first, then ask.

questions.prompt: Your friend says: “I've started volunteering at a dog shelter.” Best follow-up?
options: That's lovely! What made you decide to do it?
questions.explain: React, then ask an open question about their reason.

questions.prompt: Which is an OPEN question (it needs a longer answer)?
questions.explain: Questions with why/how/what usually need a longer answer.

questions.prompt: You didn't understand. What do you say?
options: Could you say that another way?
questions.explain: Polite and clear — asks for a reformulation.

questions.prompt: Do you ___ that the meeting is cancelled?
questions.explain: “Do you mean…?” checks your understanding.

questions.prompt: In other ___, we need more time.
questions.explain: “In other words…” introduces a simpler way to say the same thing.

questions.prompt: Let me ___ that I understood.
questions.explain: “Let me check that I understood” — check, not control.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to what it does.
pairs: Could you give me an example?
Could you say that another way?
questions.explain: These phrases help you fix misunderstandings without embarrassment.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: What I mean is…

questions.prompt: Someone says: “The office will be closed on bank holidays.” You're not sure. Best reply?
options: Do you mean public holidays like Christmas?
questions.explain: Repeat the idea in your own words to check.

questions.prompt: Which phrase introduces a simpler explanation?
questions.explain: “In other words” = I'll say it more simply.

questions.prompt: I'm hoping ___ a new job next year.
questions.explain: Hope + to + verb: I'm hoping to find…

questions.prompt: I'm thinking ___ moving to Milan.
questions.explain: Think of/about + -ing: I'm thinking of moving.

questions.prompt: My main goal is ___ improve my English.
questions.explain: Goal is + to + verb.

questions.prompt: I'm motivated ___ my children.
questions.explain: Motivated by = the reason that pushes you.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to its meaning.
questions.explain: Use these to talk about your plans and why.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: what would you like to achieve next
questions.explain: What would you like to achieve next?

questions.prompt: Your friend says: “I'm thinking of running a marathon.” Best reply?
options: Wow, great idea! What's your first step?
questions.explain: Encourage, then ask about the plan.

questions.prompt: Which sentence talks about a definite plan?
options: I'm going to start a course in January.
questions.explain: Going to = a plan you've decided.

questions.prompt: Which phrase connects to something the other person said?
questions.explain: “That reminds me of…” links your story to theirs.

questions.prompt: From my point of ___, it's better to live in the city.
questions.explain: From my point of view = in my opinion.

questions.prompt: I see what you ___.
questions.explain: “I see what you mean” shows you understand their idea.

questions.prompt: Before we change the ___, can I ask one more thing?
questions.explain: Use this to finish a topic politely.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to what it does.
questions.explain: These phrases keep a conversation flowing naturally.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: What do you think?

questions.prompt: Your friend talks about her trip to Spain. Best way to continue?
options: That reminds me of my holiday in Portugal. Did you try the food?
questions.explain: Connect, share a little, then ask a question.

questions.prompt: Which is the best way to give a reason for your opinion?
options: I prefer trains because they're relaxing.
questions.explain: Opinion + because + reason.

sets.title: B1 review: personal stories and conversation

questions.prompt: Recently, I ___ a lot about cooking.
questions.explain: Recently + present perfect for recent changes.

questions.prompt: At first I was nervous, ___ I started to enjoy it.
questions.explain: At first… then… — sequencing a story.

questions.prompt: I ___ to play the piano, but I stopped. (use)
questions.explain: Used to = past habit that stopped.

questions.prompt: Could you clarify what you ___?
questions.explain: Clarify = make clearer.

questions.prompt: Match each phrase to the lesson topic.
questions.explain: A quick tour of everything you practised at B1.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: what would you like to achieve next
questions.explain: What would you like to achieve next?

questions.prompt: Which reply keeps the conversation going best?
options: That sounds amazing! How did you feel at the end?
questions.explain: React + open follow-up question.

questions.prompt: I felt ___ when I finally passed.
questions.explain: People feel -ed: relieved.

questions.prompt: I ___ my keys. Can you help me look for them?
questions.explain: The result matters now (I still can't find them) → present perfect.

questions.prompt: We ___ to Paris in 2019.
questions.explain: A finished time (in 2019) → past simple.

questions.prompt: She ___ here since 2020.
questions.explain: “Since” + still true now → present perfect.

questions.prompt: Did you ___ (see) the match last night?
questions.explain: After “did” we use the base form: see.

questions.prompt: I've ___ (know) him for ten years.
questions.explain: Know → knew → known. After I've we need the past participle.

questions.prompt: When ___ you start learning English?
questions.explain: Questions with “when” ask about a finished time → past simple.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: I've already had lunch. “Already” goes between have and the past participle.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explain: “Yesterday” is a finished time, so we can't use the present perfect.

questions.prompt: I ___ up smoking two years ago.
questions.explain: Give up = stop doing something.

questions.prompt: We ___ out of our old flat last month.
questions.explain: Move out = leave the place where you live.

questions.prompt: She ___ up yoga during lockdown.
questions.explain: Take up = start a new hobby or activity.

questions.prompt: It took me weeks to ___ over the flu.
questions.explain: Get over = recover from an illness or a difficult experience.

questions.prompt: Match each phrasal verb to its meaning.
pairs: get used to a new place
feel happy about something in the future
questions.explain: Four very useful phrasal verbs for talking about changes in your life.

questions.prompt: I'm really looking forward ___ my holiday.
questions.explain: Look forward to + noun or -ing: I'm looking forward to seeing you.

questions.prompt: Have you settled ___ your new job yet?
questions.explain: Settle in / settle into = become comfortable in a new place or job.

questions.prompt: I need to ___ up with my old friends — I haven't seen them for ages.
questions.explain: Catch up with someone = talk and share news after some time apart.

questions.prompt: I ___ wear glasses, but now I wear contact lenses.
questions.explain: Used to for a past situation that has changed.

questions.prompt: Did you ___ live in the countryside?
questions.explain: Questions: Did you use to…?

questions.prompt: She ___ like vegetables, but now she loves them.
questions.explain: Negatives: didn't use to.

questions.prompt: We used ___ go to the beach every summer.
questions.explain: Used to + verb.

questions.prompt: He ___ to smoke, but he gave up. (use)
questions.explain: Affirmative: used to.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
questions.explain: I used to be shy.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is about now?
options: I used to work at night.
I work in the mornings now.
questions.explain: “Now” → present simple.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: I used to going to school by bus.
I used to go to school by bus.
questions.explain: Used to + base verb: go.

questions.prompt: I'm ___ in history.
questions.explain: People feel -ed: interested.

questions.prompt: This book is very ___.
questions.explain: Things that cause the feeling: -ing.

questions.prompt: The news was ___.
questions.explain: The news causes the feeling → shocking.

questions.prompt: We were ___ after the long walk.
questions.explain: How we felt → tired.

questions.prompt: The traffic was really ___.
questions.explain: The traffic causes the feeling → annoying.

questions.prompt: I was ___ (embarrass) when I forgot her name.
questions.explain: How you felt → embarrassed.

questions.prompt: The match was really ___ (excite)!
questions.explain: The match causes the feeling → exciting.

questions.prompt: Match the feeling to the meaning.
questions.explain: Useful feeling words for B1 conversations.

questions.prompt: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.explain: Going to for a prediction based on what you can see.

questions.prompt: I ___ meet Anna tomorrow at 6. It's in my diary.
questions.explain: Present continuous for fixed arrangements.

questions.prompt: “The phone's ringing.” — “I ___ answer it!”
questions.explain: Will for a quick decision made now.

questions.prompt: I'm going ___ start a new course in January.
questions.explain: Going to + verb for plans.

questions.prompt: Maybe I ___ visit London next year. (will)
questions.explain: Maybe + will for uncertain future.

questions.prompt: Match the form to its use.
questions.explain: Four common ways to talk about the future.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: what are you doing this weekend
questions.explain: What are you doing this weekend?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a fixed arrangement?
options: I'm flying to Paris on Friday.
questions.explain: Present continuous + time = arrangement.

sets.title: My first job abroad
sets.transcript: When I was twenty-three, I moved to Dublin to work in a hotel. At first, it was really hard. I understood almost nothing on the phone, and people spoke so fast! I was too shy to ask them to repeat. After about two months, my manager suggested I join an English class in the evenings. That changed everything. I made friends there, and I started speaking without worrying about mistakes. I stayed in Ireland for three years, and now I work as a receptionist in Florence. Honestly, that difficult start was the best thing that ever happened to me.

questions.prompt: Why did she move to Dublin?
questions.explain: “I moved to Dublin to work in a hotel.”

questions.prompt: What was the hardest thing at the start?
questions.explain: “I understood almost nothing on the phone.”

questions.prompt: Why didn't she ask people to repeat?
options: Her manager told her not to.
questions.explain: “I was too shy to ask them to repeat.”

questions.prompt: Who suggested the English class?
questions.explain: “My manager suggested I join an English class in the evenings.”

questions.prompt: She stayed in Ireland for ___ years.
questions.explain: “I stayed in Ireland for three years.”

questions.prompt: How does she feel about her difficult start now?
options: It was the best thing that happened to her.
She wishes she had stayed in Italy.
questions.explain: “That difficult start was the best thing that ever happened to me.”
